title: Learjet 60 charter guide
seoTitle: Learjet 60: Cabin, Range & Charter Guide | EXJET
description: Compare Learjet 60 cabin requirements, model differences and charter planning. A practical guide for executive assistants, principals and family offices.

sections.heading: When to consider the Learjet 60
paragraphs: The Learjet 60 is worth considering when a small travel party needs a business aircraft without moving into a large-cabin category. Compare the offered cabin and route plan with a Citation XLS or Hawker before choosing on price alone.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: The Learjet 60 and 60XR share a model family, but the XR designation matters when comparing avionics and aircraft specifications. Transport Canada evaluates the two together while documenting their differences. A newer interior does not turn an original 60 into a 60XR.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For a principal and assistant traveling between Dallas and a regional business center, start with the arrival deadline and work requirements. Ask for cabin photographs, the usable table arrangement and connectivity details. If several travelers need laptops open together, compare the actual seating layout rather than a passenger maximum.

For family travel, send suitcase dimensions and any golf equipment before selecting the aircraft. Ask the operator to assess the loaded itinerary, including the return flight. An attractive outbound proposal is less useful if baggage or a fuel stop changes the return plan.

sections.heading: Compare the complete charter quote
paragraphs: Request a written trip total covering the agreed itinerary, aircraft and operating carrier. Check positioning, taxes, crew expenses, airport charges and any conditional extras. Availability and price require a current proposal; this guide does not represent a live aircraft listing.

sections.heading: Plan a Learjet 60 trip
paragraphs: Send EXJET the airports, dates, local departure windows, passenger count and luggage details. Include the arrival deadline and essential cabin requirements so the options can be compared against one clear brief.

faqs.question: How does the Learjet 60 differ from the 60XR?
faqs.answer: The 60XR is a later development of the Learjet 60. Confirm the exact variant and installed avionics; a refurbished cabin alone does not establish XR specifications.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: Use this model comparison for short business visits where ground access and departure timing matter as much as flying time. Provide the meeting address so the advisor can compare convenient airports, then have the operator confirm suitability for the selected runway and conditions.

A compact cabin requires a deliberate passenger and luggage plan. Confirm full passenger seats, table positions, lavatory arrangements and bag acceptance. For a longer day of meetings, request a larger alternative if the group needs more room to work between stops.

faqs.answer: No. They are related models, but the quotation should identify the specific variant and its cabin. Do not carry seating or performance figures from one model into the other.

If the traveler count approaches the offered seating capacity, review the floor plan carefully. Confirm which seats suit a working meeting and which are appropriate for the expected flight duration. Send luggage dimensions rather than assuming one large suitcase per seat will fit.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Bombardier lists a 4,000-nautical-mile range and accommodation for up to 12 passengers for the 650. These headline figures describe the model under manufacturer conditions; they do not establish the seats, sleeping positions or nonstop capability of a particular charter.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For an assistant arranging board travel, request a floor plan showing the meeting and dining arrangement. Specify how many passengers need to work simultaneously, then confirm table space, power and connectivity. Put cabin service requirements on the same brief.

For a family office, compare a 650 with the proposed Gulfstream or Falcon alternative on the actual trip. Ask for the available rest configuration and any fuel-stop requirement. A larger maximum range is useful only if it changes the itinerary or preserves needed payload.

sections.heading: When to consider the Gulfstream GIV
paragraphs: The Gulfstream GIV is a large-cabin aircraft whose appeal is best assessed through the actual interior and trip plan. For a principal or family office, separate the value of cabin space from assumptions about age, equipment or nonstop range.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Gulfstream’s history identifies the original GIV as an intercontinental model and the GIV-SP as a later development. Its historical GIV range reference is 4,200 nautical miles. That reference does not establish route capability for a particular registration or payload.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For a business group, request the current seating and table layout, then confirm whether the cabin can support the proposed working session. Ask for the installed internet system and coverage relevant to the route; do not assume modern connectivity from a recent paint job.

For a family trip, obtain the rest layout as well as the seating plan. Ask which bags remain accessible and how service will be arranged. Compare a GIV-SP or G450 on the same passenger brief so differences in cabin condition and total cost remain clear.

faqs.answer: No. The SP is a later development. Keep the precise model and registration on the proposal and use the corresponding performance information.

paragraphs: Gulfstream describes the GIV-SP as the Special Performance development of the GIV, with increased takeoff and landing weights. The name identifies a model development; it does not establish the present interior, connectivity or maintenance condition of the aircraft offered.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For an EA coordinating a longer business trip, ask for the full cabin plan and how the principal’s preferred working and resting areas will be arranged. Confirm whether the quoted service includes a flight attendant and the requested catering.

title: Gulfstream G450 charter guide

sections.heading: When to consider the Gulfstream G450
paragraphs: The Gulfstream G450 is a large-cabin, long-range development of the GIV line. Consider it when the principal needs room for work and rest, and compare it with a GIV-SP or G550 using the actual itinerary.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Gulfstream publishes a 4,350-nautical-mile reference at Mach 0.80 with eight passengers. It is a planning benchmark, not a universal nonstop distance. The operating carrier must assess the loaded aircraft, winds, routing and required fuel reserves.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For a family office, ask for the number of usable rest positions and the arrangements for crew and cabin service. For a corporate group, check whether the table layout accommodates the people who need to work together. Both needs should be visible in the aircraft shortlist.

When the itinerary approaches the proposed aircraft’s capability, request a G550 alternative alongside the G450. Have the advisor show the expected schedule and total trip price for each. Avoid paying for additional range unless it delivers a clear journey benefit.

faqs.question: How should I compare a G450 with a G550?
faqs.answer: Start with the longest sector, passenger load and cabin needs. The G550 offers a different range capability; the operator’s itinerary assessment determines whether that advantage matters for your trip.

title: Gulfstream GV charter guide

sections.heading: When to consider the Gulfstream GV
paragraphs: The Gulfstream GV, also called the Gulfstream V, is an ultra-long-range aircraft for itineraries where time in the cabin can become a substantial part of the journey. Cabin layout, rest and service deserve the same attention as range.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Gulfstream’s historical model reference lists 6,500 nautical miles of range. That published capability should not be read as an all-payload guarantee. Ask the operator to assess the specific route and aircraft before scheduling meetings around a nonstop arrival.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For an overnight journey, request a sleeping plan that names the usable positions and explains what remains accessible during rest. Confirm cabin service, baggage access and connectivity coverage. A floor plan should make clear how the principal, accompanying travelers and crew will use the space.

For a family office considering a GV alongside a G550, compare the present cabin and installed equipment as well as the model. On an acquisition, separate the aircraft price from inspections, program participation and planned cabin work so ownership costs remain visible.

faqs.answer: Yes. GV is the commonly used abbreviation for Gulfstream V. It should still be distinguished from the later G550 in a quotation or aircraft search.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Gulfstream publishes a 6,750-nautical-mile range reference at Mach 0.80. The manufacturer also identifies enhanced Rolls-Royce BR710 engines. Treat the range as a model-level benchmark; actual payload, routing, winds and reserves determine whether a proposed trip can operate nonstop.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning

Ask for current cabin photographs and confirm internet coverage on the intended route. “Wi-Fi equipped” alone does not define speed, coverage or included usage.

For an EA managing an intercontinental itinerary, keep local arrival dates, transfers and the first appointment together. Request an operating plan that leaves room for ground formalities and any required fuel stop. Compare an alternative aircraft if the arrival deadline is fixed.

faqs.answer: No. The published figure is a comparison reference. The operator must confirm performance for the actual airports, payload, weather, routing and fuel reserves.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Transport Canada’s Global-family material distinguishes aircraft marketed under the Global Express, XRS, 5000 and 6000 names. A common family does not mean the same flight deck, cabin equipment or performance. Request the exact variant and registration at the proposal stage.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For a family office, begin with the overnight arrangement: usable sleeping positions, separation between areas and access to luggage. Ask how the cabin will function when some passengers are resting and others need to work or receive service.

paragraphs: The Global Express XRS, often shortened to Global XRS, is an ultra-long-range aircraft to compare with the original Global Express and Global 6000. Focus the selection on the complete journey and the aircraft’s present cabin.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Transport Canada identifies the XRS with Honeywell avionics and distinguishes the Global 6000 with the Global Vision flight deck. These names should not be merged into a single specification in a charter or acquisition proposal.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For a principal crossing several time zones, ask for a cabin plan that supports uninterrupted rest as well as service. Specify who needs a separate work area and how many sleeping positions are essential. Verify the actual arrangement rather than relying on maximum passenger capacity.

For an EA, prepare the itinerary in local dates and times and include the first destination appointment. Request a complete route assessment, including any fuel stop and ground transfer. Compare the XRS with a 6000 only after the required cabin features are confirmed.

sections.heading: When to consider the Falcon 2000
paragraphs: The Falcon 2000 is a wide-cabin twin-engine aircraft family that deserves precise variant identification. For executive teams and family offices, the offered cabin can be as important as the distinction between the original aircraft and later developments.

paragraphs: Dassault describes the original Falcon 2000 as a transcontinental twinjet. Later names such as 2000EX, LX and LXS identify developments within the family. The current 2000LXS range should not be used as the specification for an original Falcon 2000.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For a corporate party, request a layout showing the dining or meeting table and the seats around it. Confirm how the cabin works when several passengers need laptops and others want to rest. Ask for current photographs and installed connectivity details.

paragraphs: The Falcon 900 family offers a large-cabin option for business and family travel. Selection begins with the exact variant: an original 900, 900B, 900EX or 900LX should not be represented by one generic performance specification.

sections.heading: Model and performance reference
paragraphs: Dassault traces the Falcon 900 to a larger and wider development of the Falcon 50 and identifies the 900EX as a later version. The three-engine layout is a defining family feature, but engine count alone does not establish the suitability of a charter or guarantee any route.

sections.heading: Cabin and itinerary planning
paragraphs: For a principal traveling with colleagues or family, review the actual floor plan for separate activities. Confirm which seats convert for rest and how catering will be delivered without disrupting that arrangement. Ask for luggage acceptance using the full trip’s requirements.

For a longer international flight, compare the proposed variant’s route assessment with a G450 or Challenger 650 alternative. If the aircraft is being considered for ownership, make the records review and model-specific inspection scope part of the acquisition brief.

paragraphs: Send EXJET the airports, dates, local departure windows, passenger count and luggage details. Include the arrival deadline and essential cabin requirements so the options can be compared against one clear brief.
